subject: Chemistry
chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
title: Functional Groups
summary: Two molecules can share the same carbon chain and still behave differently. How one small group of atoms gives a compound its chemical identity: –OH, –CHO, C=O, –COOH and –NH₂.
keyPoints: A **functional group** is an atom or group of atoms that largely decides a compound's characteristic chemical properties and reactions.
Think of it this way: the **carbon chain** is the body, the **functional group** is the identity.
**–OH** alcohol, **–CHO** aldehyde, **C=O** in the middle of a chain ketone, **–COOH** carboxylic acid, **–NH₂** amine.
An aldehyde and a ketone both have C=O. In an aldehyde it is at the end of the chain, with an H on it.
Compounds with the same group react alike, so learn groups, not single molecules.

blocks.p: Keep the chain CH₃CH₂– and change only the group. The carbon in –CHO and –COOH belongs to the group, so the chain stays the same.
Propanoic acid fizzes with sodium hydrogencarbonate and gives CO₂. Ethanol does not, even though both carry the same chain. That difference comes from the group.
The group does not decide everything. Longer chains still change physical properties such as boiling point: ethanol boils at about 78 °C and propan-1-ol at about 97 °C.

quiz.q: A functional group is best described as:
options: an atom or group of atoms that largely decides a compound's chemical properties
any hydrogen atom in a molecule
quiz.explain: It can be one atom or several, and it gives the compound its characteristic reactions.
–CHO at the end of a chain marks an aldehyde.

quiz.q: How is a ketone different from an aldehyde?
options: In a ketone, C=O sits between two carbon atoms
quiz.explain: Both have C=O, but an aldehyde's is at the chain end with an H attached.
A carboxylic acid is acidic enough to release CO₂.
–NH₂ is the group of a primary amine.

simulation.reason: That the group, not the chain, decides a reaction is a hypothesis students can test: changing the chain leaves each test result the same while changing the group changes it, and the boiling point still moves with the chain, which shows why the group only largely decides.
simulation.objective: Change the chain and the group separately and find which one decides each test result.
instructions: Build a molecule from a chain and a group.
Run a test and read the result.
Keep the group, change the chain, and run the same test.
Keep the chain, change the group, and run it again.
Compare the boiling points as the chain grows.
